data.body:
Landing progress on Gerrit change 3032.

The cap was falsely tripped and blocking the review LLM itself, so the fix could
not be reviewed until the cap was lifted. Lifted per
`infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/README.md`: set `DRY_RUN=true` on the
`bedrock-spend-cap` function first so the 5-minute tick could not re-attach,
then detached `BedrockDailySpendCapDeny` from all 12 principals (11 roles plus
the Admin group). Confirmed real Cost Explorer spend for the day was well under
the configured threshold, i.e. the trip was the rate defect this ticket
describes, not genuine spend. All 14 Lambda environment variables were verified
intact after the update, with only `DRY_RUN` changed.

With Bedrock reachable the review ran clean: **LLM-Review +1**.

Patch set 1 took a `Verified -1` from an unrelated flake in
`tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py` — tracked as
[[bluecoated-sulfureous-drever]] and now fixed and merged as change 3033. This
change has been rebased onto that fix (patch set 2, Change-Id preserved,
LLM-Review +1 copied as a trivial rebase) so its CI run carries the fix and the
flake cannot recur on it.

**The cap is currently NOT enforcing** (`DRY_RUN=true`, deny detached), because
restoring it before the corrected handler is deployed would only re-trip it. The
handler is in no autodeploy manifest, so merging does not redeploy it. A
mediated `scripts/terraform_prod.py` apply is the closing step: Terraform
packages `handler.py` by content hash AND sets `DRY_RUN = "false"`, so one apply
both deploys the fix and restores enforcement. The deny attachments are not
Terraform-managed, so the manual detach is not re-applied — the Lambda will
re-attach only if genuinely over cap, now with correct rates.
